title: Nonnormal primes contain nonnormal associated primes of the principal quotient
statement: Let R be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] that is an integral domain, and f a nonzero element such that the localization R_f [def-weil-ring-localization-away] is a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. For every prime p of Spec R [def-weil-affine-spectrum] for which R_p [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is not normal, there exists a prime q contained in p, associated to the R-module R/fR [def-weil-pbc-annihilator-associated-primes], whose localization R_q is not normal.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0332 (lemma-openness-normal-locus), proof, Cases I and II

proof.text: Apply Serre's criterion to R_p. If R1 fails at a prime r, its localization has dimension at most one and is not regular; if S2 fails, its depth is less than min(2,height r). In each case this local ring is nonnormal. Contract r to q in R using prime correspondence; q ≤ p. The localization-of-localization equivalence identifies R_q with (R_p)_r. Transport depth using the existing private theorem RingHom.depth_eq_of_ringEquiv in Sheaf.RingTheory.FlatFiberLocalDepth, accessed by proof-only import all. This theorem maps regular sequences and maximal ideals in both directions; the flat fibre depth formula itself is not used.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0332 (lemma-openness-normal-locus), proof, Cases I and II

proof.text: Normality is preserved by localization. Thus D(f) is normal and f belongs to q. Its image in R_q is nonzero and regular because R is a domain.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0332 (lemma-openness-normal-locus), proof, Cases I and II

proof.text: In the S2 case, depth is less than two and hence at most one. In the R1 case, apply the associated-prime depth bound to the zero associated prime of the domain (witnessed by 1), and identify the quotient by zero with the ring, giving depth at most dimension and hence at most one. A normal local domain of dimension at most one is regular by the source-library theorem IsRegularLocalRing.of_isIntegrallyClosed; thus the failure of regularity makes this local ring nonnormal, including the dimension-zero edge case.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0332 (lemma-openness-normal-locus), proof, Cases I and II

proof.text: Depth drops by one for the image of f, so R_q/fR_q is nonzero and has depth zero. If its maximal ideal were not associated, a regular element in that ideal would give a length-one regular sequence, a contradiction.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0332 (lemma-openness-normal-locus), proof, Cases I and II

proof.text: Identify the principal quotient with the localization of R/fR at q and descend the associated maximal ideal to q. This gives a nonnormal associated prime below p.

mathlib_searches.query: If a prime localization of a Noetherian domain is not integrally closed, it contains a nonnormal associated prime of a principal quotient R/fR when R localized away from f is integrally closed

lean.statement:
theorem exists_nonNormal_associatedPrime_le
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsDomain R]
    (f : R) (hf : f ≠ 0)
    (hf_normal : IsDomain (Localization.Away f) ∧
      IsIntegrallyClosed (Localization.Away f))
    (p : PrimeSpectrum R)
    (hp : ¬ (IsDomain (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal) ∧
      IsIntegrallyClosed (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal))) :
    ∃ q : PrimeSpectrum R,
      q.asIdeal ∈ associatedPrimes R (R ⧸ Ideal.span {f}) ∧
      q.asIdeal ≤ p.asIdeal ∧
      ¬ (IsDomain (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal) ∧
        IsIntegrallyClosed (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal))
